# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Worker script for the free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel; its `wrangler.jsonc` lives at the repository root. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding" # outcome-format check agentic-odi guidelines # the ODI stage-by-stage guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can do agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. 1: # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
2: 
3: This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
4: 
5: > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
10: 
11: This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
12: 
13: ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
14: 
15: ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
16: 
17: ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
22: 
23: - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
24: - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
25: - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
26: - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
31: 
32: - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
33: - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
34: - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
35: 
36:   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
37: 
38:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
39:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
40:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
41:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
42: 
43: - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
48: 
49: - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
50:   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
51:   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
52:   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
53:   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
54:   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
55:   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
56:   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
57:   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
58: 
59: - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
60: - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
65: 
66: - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
67:   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
68:   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
69: 
70: - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
71: 
72:   ```
73:   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
74:   ```
75: 
76: - **Interpretation**:
77:   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
78:   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
79:   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
80: 
81: - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
86: 
87: - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
88: - Segments can be:
89:   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
90:   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
91:   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
92: 
93: - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
98: 
99: Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
100: 
101: | Strategy | When to use |
102: |---|---|
103: | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
104: | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
105: | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
106:

# Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

- **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.

---

### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

description: Start the local dev stack and run end-to-end tests against the Living Studio SPA
---

# Local Dev & Test Workflow

Use this workflow whenever the user asks to:
- Run the app locally
- Test the agent/server/client stack end-to-end
- Open the browser and interact with the Living Studio SPA

## Steps

1. **Start the server** — Launch the FastMCP server and the Living Studio sidecar as a
   single background process using the dev launcher.

   ```
   uv run python scripts/dev.py
   ```

   Run with `WaitMsBeforeAsync: 2000` so the server has time to bind its port before
   continuing. Save the CommandId as `SERVER_CMD`.

2. **Verify the server is healthy** — Check `SERVER_CMD` status. If it has exited with an
   error, stop and report the error to the user. Do not proceed.

3. **Verify the studio is running** — Confirm the studio sidecar has started by checking
   for the "Living Studio" URL printout (`http://localhost:8100`).

4. **Open the browser** — Use the `browser_subagent` tool to navigate to
   `http://localhost:8100` and visually confirm the Living Studio SPA loads correctly.

5. **Run end-to-end interaction** — Use `browser_subagent` to exercise a feature
   (e.g., explore the Opportunity Landscape or query job maps) and confirm the UI
   responds correctly. Report what you see.

6. **Report results** — Use `notify_user` to summarize:
   - Whether the MCP server and studio sidecar started cleanly
   - What the browser showed
   - Any errors encountered

7. **Teardown (when done)** — Terminate `SERVER_CMD` using `send_command_input` with
   `Terminate: true`.

## Notes

- The MCP server runs on `http://localhost:8000/mcp`
- The Living Studio runs on `http://localhost:8100`
- All commands should be run from the project root (the `agentic-odi` workspace root).
- The MCP server does not require an LLM. The studio SPA is a static build; if the
  frontend is not built, the dev launcher prints a hint with the build command.

 # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
 
 This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
 
 > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
 
 This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
 
 ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
 
 ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
 
 ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
 
 - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
 - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
 - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
 - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
 
 - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
 - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
 - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
 
   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
 
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
 
 - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
 
 - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
 - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
 
 - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
 
 - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
 
   ```
   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
   ```
 
 - **Interpretation**:
   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
 
 - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
 - Segments can be:
   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
 
 Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
 
 | Strategy | When to use |
 |---|---|
 | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
 | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
 | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
 
 ---
 
 ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
 
 These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
 
 | DO | DON'T |
 |---|---|
 | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
 | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
 | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
 | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
 | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
 | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
 | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

 - **Language**: Python 3.10+
 - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)

 `README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# score.sh — Native GitHub Action PR risk classifier.
+#
+# Evaluates a pull request diff across three factors and applies a single,
+# mutually exclusive risk label. Runs entirely on ubuntu-latest with git + gh
+# (both preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners). Zero external SaaS, zero API
+# keys, zero PR comments.
+#
+# Factors (0-100 score):
+#   1. File & line churn        -> 0-30 points
+#   2. Critical path override   -> forces danger zone (>= 51)
+#   3. Test delta               -> +20 if source changed without test files
+#
+# Tiers:
+#   <= 20  -> safe to merge     (🟢)
+#   21-50  -> needs a look      (🟡)
+#   >= 51  -> danger zone       (🔴)
+#
+# Env required: GITHUB_TOKEN, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA, PR_NUMBER, REPO
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Configuration
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+readonly RISK_LABELS=("safe to merge" "needs a look" "danger zone")
+readonly CRITICAL_PREFIXES=("auth/" "migrations/" "billing/" "infra/" ".github/workflows/")
+readonly PROTECTED_FILES_FILE=".ci/protected-files.txt"
+
+# Score thresholds
+readonly CHURN_FILES_MAX=10      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_MAX=20      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_CAP=400     # lines at which line-points saturate
+readonly TEST_DELTA_POINTS=20
+readonly DANGER_FLOOR=51
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is a test file: *.test.*, *.spec.*, or under tests/
+is_test_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  [[ "${f}" == *.test.* || "${f}" == *.spec.* ]] && return 0
+  [[ "${f}" == tests/* || "${f}" == */tests/* ]] && return 0
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is source code worth test coverage (excludes docs,
+# configs, static assets, lockfiles, etc.). Test delta only fires on these.
+is_source_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  local ext="${f##*.}"
+  case "${ext}" in
+    py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|go|rs|rb|java|c|cpp|h|hpp|cs|php|swift|kt|scala|r|m|mm|sh|bash|zsh|tf|vue|dart|lua|ex|exs|erl|hs|ml|clj|cljs|sql|graphql|proto) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  local base="${f##*/}"
+  case "${base}" in
+    Dockerfile|dockerfile|Makefile|makefile|Gemfile|Rakefile|Vagrantfile|BUILD|BUILD.bazel|WORKSPACE|configure|Configure) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Gather diff between base and head
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# All changed files (Added / Copied / Modified / Deleted)
+CHANGED_FILES="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMD "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+# Shortstat for churn counts
+STAT="$(git diff --shortstat "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+LINES_ADDED=0
+LINES_DELETED=0
+if [[ -n "${STAT}" ]]; then
+  FILES_CHANGED_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ file' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_ADDED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ insertion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_DELETED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ deletion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+fi
+[[ -z "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" ]] && FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_ADDED}" ]] && LINES_ADDED=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_DELETED}" ]] && LINES_DELETED=0
+readonly TOTAL_LINES=$((LINES_ADDED + LINES_DELETED))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 1: File & line churn (0-30)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+score=0
+
+# Files changed: 1 point per file, capped at CHURN_FILES_MAX
+if [[ "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" -ge "${CHURN_FILES_MAX}" ]]; then
+  churn_files="${CHURN_FILES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_files="${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_files))
+
+# Lines changed: linear up to CHURN_LINES_MAX at CHURN_LINES_CAP lines
+if [[ "${TOTAL_LINES}" -ge "${CHURN_LINES_CAP}" ]]; then
+  churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_lines=$((TOTAL_LINES * CHURN_LINES_MAX / CHURN_LINES_CAP))
+  [[ "${churn_lines}" -gt "${CHURN_LINES_MAX}" ]] && churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_lines))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 2: Critical path override (blast radius)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+critical_touch=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  for prefix in "${CRITICAL_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
+    if [[ "${f}" == "${prefix}"* ]]; then
+      critical_touch=1
+      break 2
+    fi
+  done
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+# Deletions of protected CI/site files also count as critical.
+if [[ -f "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}" && -n "${CHANGED_FILES}" ]]; then
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+    # Only consider deletions: a file in the diff that no longer exists at HEAD
+    if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}:${f}" 2>/dev/null; then
+      while IFS= read -r p; do
+        [[ -z "${p}" || "${p}" == \#* ]] && continue
+        if [[ "${f}" == "${p}" ]]; then
+          critical_touch=1
+          break 2
+        fi
+      done < "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}"
+    fi
+  done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 3: Test delta (+20 if source changed without test files)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+source_changed=0
+test_changed=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  if is_test_file "${f}"; then
+    test_changed=1
+  elif is_source_file "${f}"; then
+    source_changed=1
+  fi
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+if [[ "${source_changed}" -eq 1 && "${test_changed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  score=$((score + TEST_DELTA_POINTS))
+fi
+
+# Apply critical-path floor
+if [[ "${critical_touch}" -eq 1 && "${score}" -lt "${DANGER_FLOOR}" ]]; then
+  score="${DANGER_FLOOR}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Determine tier (mutually exclusive)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ "${score}" -le 20 ]]; then
+  tier="safe to merge"
+elif [[ "${score}" -le 50 ]]; then
+  tier="needs a look"
+else
+  tier="danger zone"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Label hygiene: remove all stale risk labels, then apply the current tier.
+# No PR comments are posted (silent execution).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+for label in "${RISK_LABELS[@]}"; do
+  gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --remove-label "${label}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+done
+gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --add-label "${tier}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+
+echo "PR risk score: ${score}/100 -> ${tier}"

+name: Label merge conflicts
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 */6 * * *'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+  pull-requests: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: label-merge-conflicts-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  label-merge-state:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Ensure labels exist
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          gh label create merge-conflict --color b60205 \
+            --description "Pull request has merge conflicts" --force || true
+          gh label create merge-ready --color 28a745 \
+            --description "Pull request merges cleanly into main" --force || true
+
+      - name: Collect target PR numbers
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
+            echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"
+          else
+            gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --base main \
+              --state open --json number -q '.[].number' \
+              > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Label each PR by merge state
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          while IFS= read -r number; do
+            [ -z "$number" ] && continue
+            state="$(gh pr view "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+              --json mergeStateStatus -q '.mergeStateStatus')"
+            case "$state" in
+              dirty)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --add-label merge-conflict >/dev/null
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-ready >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+              clean)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --add-label merge-ready >/dev/null
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-conflict >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+              *)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-conflict >/dev/null || true
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-ready >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+            esac
+            echo "PR #$number: $state"
+          done < "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"

To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | -| **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | +| **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The conversation runs on **assistant-ui** — streaming, reasoning, tool calls, approvals, sources, attachments, branches, and suggestions are the library's runtime; the ODI intelligence and the **agent-composed surfaces** (scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations) are ours, from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Worker script for the free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel; its `wrangler.jsonc` lives at the repository root. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. +The thread behaves like a real assistant surface, not a chat box. Replies stream; +reasoning arrives as a collapsed disclosure rather than prose; each tool call is a +trace chip with the source the turn actually read; a write to your data pauses for +a **Yes/No** before it runs; text and image attachments ride along with the turn; +and any reply can be edited or regenerated as a **branch** you step through with +`‹ 2 of 3 ›`. Starter suggestions change with the canvas. The runtime underneath +is [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com); the ODI surfaces, the catalog, +and the sidecar contract stay ours. + The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding" # outcome-format check agentic-odi guidelines # the ODI stage-by-stage guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can do agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`.  def update_cmd(
     check: bool = False,
     force: bool = False,
     version: str | None = None,
     now: bool = False,
 ) -> None:
     """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
     if check:
         latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
         if latest is None:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
         return
 
     if not paths.is_frozen():
         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
         return
 
     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
     if target is None:
         if force:
             target = __version__
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
             return
 
     try:
         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
             archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
         typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc
 
     typer.echo(f"Updated to v{target}")
     if now:
         _reexec_current()

+"""Long tools report progress so the Studio can stop looking hung."""

+
+import json

+
+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server import mcp
+from fastmcp import Client

+
+async def _collect_progress(client: Client, tool: str, arguments: dict) -> tuple[object, list]:
+    events: list[tuple[float, float | None, str | None]] = []
+
+    async def on_progress(progress: float, total: float | None, message: str | None) -> None:
+        events.append((progress, total, message))
+
+    result = await client.call_tool(tool, arguments, progress_handler=on_progress)
+    return result, events
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_evaluate_outcome_reports_progress_before_returning() -> None:

+        )

+    assert json.loads(cast(Any, result).content[0].text)["valid"] is True
+    assert events
+    assert events[-1][0] == events[-1][1]
+    assert events[-1][2] == "Evaluation complete"
+
+

+"""In-process approval gates for mutating tool calls.
+
+A mutating MCP tool (``add_job``, ``update_outcome``, …) pauses the streaming
+turn until the person in front of the Studio says yes or no. The gate is a
+process-local registry of pending futures: the SSE generator awaits one, and
+``POST /api/approvals/{id}`` resolves it.
+
+This is deliberately the smallest thing that is honest. The sidecar serves one
+local user over one loopback socket; it has no durable job state and no worker
+pool, so a gate that lives in memory is the whole requirement. Every gate has a
+timeout and every gate resolves once, so a turn can never hang and a double
+click can never run a tool twice.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import threading
+import uuid
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+#: A person deciding whether the agent may write to their data deserves longer
+#: than a network timeout, but the turn must still end on its own.
+DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalRequest:
+    """One pending decision, described well enough for the UI to ask."""
+
+    id: str
+    tool_call_id: str
+    name: str
+    arguments: dict[str, object]
+    prompt: str
+    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
+        return {
+            "id": self.id,
+            "tool_call_id": self.tool_call_id,
+            "name": self.name,
+            "arguments": self.arguments,
+            "prompt": self.prompt,
+            "created_at": self.created_at,
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalDecision:
+    approved: bool
+    reason: str = ""
+
+
+class ApprovalNotFoundError(KeyError):
+    """No pending gate has that id, or it already resolved."""
+
+
+class ApprovalRegistry:
+    """Pending approval gates, keyed by the id the client answers with."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._pending: dict[str, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]] = {}
+
+    def open(
+        self,
+        *,
+        tool_call_id: str,
+        name: str,
+        arguments: dict[str, object],
+        prompt: str,
+    ) -> tuple[ApprovalRequest, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]]:
+        """Register a gate and return its description and the future to await."""
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        request = ApprovalRequest(
+            id=f"apv_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}",
+            tool_call_id=tool_call_id,
+            name=name,
+            arguments=arguments,
+            prompt=prompt,
+        )
+        future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision] = loop.create_future()
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending[request.id] = future
+        return request, future
+
+    def resolve(self, approval_id: str, decision: ApprovalDecision) -> None:
+        """Answer a pending gate. Raises when the gate is unknown or already closed."""
+        with self._lock:
+            future = self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+        if future is None or future.done():
+            raise ApprovalNotFoundError(approval_id)
+        future.set_result(decision)
+
+    def discard(self, approval_id: str) -> None:
+        """Forget a gate without answering it (the turn ended first)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+
+    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
+        """Drop every pending gate. Called when the sidecar shuts down."""
+        with self._lock:
+            pending = list(self._pending.items())
+            self._pending.clear()
+        for _approval_id, future in pending:
+            if not future.done():
+                future.cancel()
+
+    @property
+    def pending(self) -> int:
+        with self._lock:
+            return len(self._pending)
+
+
+async def wait_for_decision(
+    registry: ApprovalRegistry,
+    request: ApprovalRequest,
+    future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision],
+    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+) -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+    """Await a decision, returning ``None`` when the gate expired or was dropped.
+
+    The gate is always discarded, so an expired id can never be answered later
+    and a cancelled turn leaves nothing behind.
+    """
+    try:
+        return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
+    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+        return None
+    except asyncio.CancelledError:
+        raise
+    finally:
+        registry.discard(request.id)
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ApprovalDecision",
+    "ApprovalNotFoundError",
+    "ApprovalRegistry",
+    "ApprovalRequest",
+    "DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS",
+    "wait_for_decision",
+]

     events: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

         for line in block.splitlines():
             if line.startswith("event: "):
                 name = line[len("event: ") :]

         if name and data is not None:

+"""The write-approval gate: it resolves once, expires, and never leaks."""
+

+
+import asyncio
+import json
+
+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.approvals import (
+    ApprovalDecision,
+    ApprovalNotFoundError,
+    ApprovalRegistry,
+    wait_for_decision,
+)
+
+
+def _open(registry: ApprovalRegistry) -> tuple[object, object]:
+    async def _run() -> tuple[object, object]:
+        return registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1",
+            name="add_job",
+            arguments={"name": "Retention"},
+            prompt="Allow the assistant to add job?",
+        )
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_open_describes_the_call_for_the_ui() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+    request, _future = _open(registry)
+
+    payload = request.to_dict()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+
+    assert payload["id"].startswith("apv_")
+    assert payload["tool_call_id"] == "call-1"
+    assert payload["name"] == "add_job"
+    assert payload["arguments"] == {"name": "Retention"}
+    assert payload["prompt"] == "Allow the assistant to add job?"
+    assert registry.pending == 1
+
+
+def test_resolve_answers_the_waiting_turn() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        pending = asyncio.create_task(wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=5))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True, reason="ok"))
+        decision = await pending
+        assert decision is not None
+        return decision
+
+    decision = asyncio.run(_run())
+
+    assert decision.approved is True
+    assert decision.reason == "ok"
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_an_expired_gate_returns_none_and_is_forgotten() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        return await wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=0.01)
+
+    assert asyncio.run(_run()) is None
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_a_gate_answers_only_once() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> None:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True))
+        with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):
+            registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=False))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        assert future.done()
+
+    asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_an_unknown_gate_cannot_be_resolved() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):
+        registry.resolve("apv_missing", ApprovalDecision(approved=True))
+
+
+def test_cancel_all_drops_every_pending_gate() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> list[bool]:
+        _first, first_future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        _second, second_future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-2", name="delete_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        registry.cancel_all()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        return [first_future.cancelled(), second_future.cancelled()]
+
+    assert asyncio.run(_run()) == [True, True]
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_the_decision_serializes_for_the_stream() -> None:
+    decision = ApprovalDecision(approved=False, reason="not this time")
+
+    assert json.loads(json.dumps(decision.__dict__)) == {
+        "approved": False,
+        "reason": "not this time",
+    }

+def _parse(frames: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
+    events: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        name = None
+        data = None
+        for line in frame.splitlines():
+            if line.startswith("event: "):
+                name = line[len("event: ") :]
+            elif line.startswith("data: "):
+                data = line[len("data: ") :]
+        if name and data is not None:
+            events.append((name, json.loads(data)))
+    return events
+
+
+def _collect(request: ChatRequest, approvals: ApprovalRegistry | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    async def _run() -> list[str]:
+        return [frame async for frame in chat.stream_chat(request, approvals=approvals)]
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def _collect_answering(
+    request: ChatRequest,
+    approvals: ApprovalRegistry,
+    decision: ApprovalDecision,
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Consume the turn, answering the first approval gate that appears."""
+
+    async def _run() -> list[str]:
+        frames: list[str] = []
+        async for frame in chat.stream_chat(request, approvals=approvals):
+            frames.append(frame)
+            if frame.startswith("event: approval"):
+                payload = json.loads(frame.split("data: ", 1)[1])
+                approvals.resolve(payload["id"], decision)
+        return frames
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+

+        """
+        CREATE TABLE conversations (
+            id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+            created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+        );
+        CREATE TABLE turns (
+            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

+        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
+            VALUES ('c1', 'user', 'hello', 'now');
+        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
+            VALUES ('c1', 'assistant', 'hi', 'now');

 # Repository Architecture
 
 Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.
 
 ## Layout
 
 ```text
 apps/
   cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
   mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
   studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
   studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
 packages/
   core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
   connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
 infra/cloudflare/ Worker script; wrangler.jsonc lives at the repo root
 scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
 tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
 docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
 packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
 ```
 
 ## Dependency Direction
 
 ```text
 apps/cli ──────────────┐
 apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
 apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
                                  │
 apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
 ```
 
 - `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
 - `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
 - Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
 - The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
+- The SPA's conversation runtime is assistant-ui, bound to the Studio's own
+  store in `apps/studio/src/assistant/`. That directory
+  is the whole bridge: `convert.ts` maps the two message models in both
+  directions, `StudioRuntime.tsx` wires the runtime callbacks, and
+  `attachments.ts` extracts files in the browser. The library is presentation
+  only — it holds no product state and makes no network calls of its own.
 
 ## Persistence
 
 - `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
 - The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
 - Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
   `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
   sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
 - `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
 - The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
 - The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.
 
 ## MCP Contract
 
 `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.
 
 ## Entry Points
 
 | Command | Module |
 |---|---|
 | `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
 | `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
 | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
 | `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |
 
 ## Related
 
 - [Data flow](data-flow.md)
 - [Testing](testing.md)
